title: OpenAIRE Graph — software
cite_as: Manghi, P. et al. OpenAIRE Research Graph Dump (v3.0), Zenodo, 2021. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4707307
description: The **software** slice of the 2021 OpenAIRE Graph: 221,817 research software records as one range-queryable graph.

- One `oaire:Software` per record, with title, publication year (`xsd:gYear`), issue date, publisher, language, best access right (`OPEN`, `RESTRICTED`, `CLOSED`, `EMBARGO`), subjects (`dct:subject`), venue and links to full text (`oaire:fulltextUrl`).

- **Reified authorship.** `oaire:hasAuthor` points at an `oaire:AuthorRole` with an `oaire:rank`, held (`oaire:isHeldBy`) by an `oaire:Agent`. That makes "second author of X" a question the graph can answer.

- **Joins by IRI, not by string.** A record with a DOI *is* `https://doi.org/{doi}`, and an author with an ORCID *is* `https://orcid.org/{id}`. This shard therefore federates with crossref, datacite, opencitations, dblp and orcid. Everything else keeps its OpenAIRE id under `https://w3id.org/rete/openaire/50/…`.

Source: the **OpenAIRE Research Graph Dump v3.0** (Zenodo [10.5281/zenodo.4707307](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4707307), published 2021-04-27, CC BY 4.0), converted to Parquet on 2026-07-15 with `scripts/openaire/tars_to_parquet.py` (19 source tars matched by name and size, zero bad lines), then to N-Triples by `scripts/openaire/parquet_to_nt.py --only software`. Vocabulary `oaire:` = <https://w3id.org/rete/openaire#>.

Rebuilt with `rete build - --strict --memory-budget-mb 1500 --no-pyramid`. `--strict` refuses any IRI the N-Triples grammar or RFC 3987 rejects, so every IRI here loads into a strict triple store as-is. Free-text URLs (`instance.url`) are percent-escaped where escaping keeps their meaning, repaired where the value itself states a scheme but mispunctuates it (`http//x`), and otherwise **dropped and counted**: an empty URL (the 2021 build wrote these as the IRI `<>`), a bare host with no scheme, a value that is not a URL at all, or an authority RFC 3987 rejects. Minted DOI IRIs carry the same escaping `rete export --sanitize-iris` applies, so an IRI that was already valid is unchanged.
The converter prints its tally on every run. It never adds a scheme to a value that does not state one, and it never rewrites a host.
example_queries:
# Authors with an ORCID, in rank order on their record
PREFIX oaire: <https://w3id.org/rete/openaire#>
SELECT ?record ?rank ?author WHERE {
  ?record oaire:hasAuthor ?role .
  ?role oaire:rank ?rank ; oaire:isHeldBy ?author .
  FILTER(STRSTARTS(STR(?author), "https://orcid.org/"))
} LIMIT 20
